all_questions.question: [actigraphy / behavioral medicine] Is an ISLES'24 raw-CTP model using residual patient head motion -- restlessness written into the 4D time series -- as a prognostic cue?

[control engineering / queueing theory] Is an ISLES'24 model using the autoregulatory blood-volume reserve -- CBV held up while CBF falls, Little's law read across the perfusion maps -- to separate salvageable from lost tissue?

[statistical physics: percolation] Is an ISLES'24 model using the percolation state of the hypoperfusion field -- one spanning cluster versus scattered islands -- beyond the deficit's volume and severity?
[hydraulic engineering: Windkessel] Is an ISLES'24 model using the exponential tail of the arterial input function as an arterial-stiffness clock -- the patient's vascular age read from one curve?
[acoustics: room impulse response] Is an ISLES'24 model using the recirculation echo -- the bolus's second pass -- as a whole-body cardiac-output clock inside a brain scan?
[seismology: travel-time tomography] Is an ISLES'24 model using the spatial gradient of contrast arrival time -- tissue filling backward from the cortical surface -- as a collateral-flow compass?
[actuarial science: frailty indices] Is an ISLES'24 model using ventricular-and-sulcal CSF fraction on NCCT -- brain age -- as an actuarial prior on tissue survival?
[reliability engineering: N+1 redundancy] Is an ISLES'24 model using Circle-of-Willis completeness from the released CoW masks as a single-point-of-failure analysis of the patient's arterial supply?

dropped.why: There is exactly one AIF per case, so no within-case contrast exists, and across cases the tail's decay constant is inseparable from injection protocol and cardiac output -- the precise IDENTIFIABILITY_FAILURE pattern that killed idea-016; no design was found that breaks it.

dropped.why: Retrograde filling direction is collateral supply measured with a new instrument; cycle isles24-001 already owns the collateral question (c01 collateral clock, c02 vascular detour), so this spends a wide slot re-instrumenting an old X rather than widening the space.

dropped.why: Adjacent to isles24-scout-001-c04 (the frail brain around the threatened territory); the atrophy-versus-leukoaraiosis delta is real but thin, and the frailty-prior grammar feeds conditional-observational, already the portfolio's most concentrated template (x12).

candidates.title: The scan is also an actigraph: the model may be reading how much the patient moved
candidates.question: Is an ISLES'24 raw-CTP model using residual patient head motion in the 4D time series -- restlessness written into the acquisition -- as a prognostic cue?

cross_field.borrowed_construct: Actigraphy / behavioral medicine: movement as a vital sign -- agitation, neglect, and impaired compliance are behavioral severity measures, routinely quantified by accelerometry in delirium and stroke-unit monitoring.
cross_field.instrument_it_implies: Framewise displacement (FD), the head-motion instrument from fMRI quality control (Power et al., NeuroImage 2012, PMID 22019881), transplanted to CTP: the scan itself becomes an actigraph.
cross_field.what_changes_if_dropped: Nothing about the measurement (FD stands alone); the actigraphy frame supplies the causal reading -- motion as behavior, not noise -- and the named clinical failure mode.

causal_chain.link: L1: More severe cortical deficits (aphasia, neglect, agitation) impair compliance and produce more head motion during the roughly minute-long CTP acquisition.
causal_chain.separately_checkable_by: Correlate the automated motion index against released admission NIHSS across all 149 cases (clinical CSV is in the release). Honestly contested: Fahmi et al. 2013 reported motion largely independent of neurological condition at their grading, while a 2021 Eur J Radiol follow-up studied correlation with baseline features (paywalled today, direction unretrieved); L1 is therefore a preregistered in-dataset test, not an assumption.

causal_chain.link: L2: The organizers' motion correction removed gross displacement but left a measurable, patient-gradeable residue (frame-to-frame inconsistency, interpolation blur).
causal_chain.separately_checkable_by: FD and temporal-inconsistency census on the released corrected series -- the keystone gate.

causal_chain.link: L3: A model trained on raw CTP absorbs the residue as a prior on outcome.
causal_chain.separately_checkable_by: The motion-injection intervention below -- this is the use claim.

causal_chain.link: Z (implied failure mode): sedated or intubated severe-stroke patients, who lie still, get systematically under-predicted lesions; agitated patients with mild strokes get over-predicted ones -- a bias invisible to every leaderboard metric.
causal_chain.separately_checkable_by: If L1-L3 hold, stratify model residuals by the motion index at matched deficit burden.

candidates.deliverable_sentence: The raw-CTP model is using the residual patient-motion signature in the time series -- restlessness the correction step could not fully erase -- as a prognostic cue when it predicts final infarct extent.
candidates.X_measurement: Framewise displacement adapted from fMRI QC: rigidly re-register each 1 frame/s CTP frame to the series median (SimpleITK/elastix, automatic), FD = summed absolute translations plus rotations converted to 50-mm-arc displacements per frame transition; case-level index = mean and 95th-percentile FD, plus a temporal-inconsistency energy (median absolute frame-to-frame difference in registered space) capturing interpolation residue that re-registration cannot undo. Amplitude context from Fahmi et al. 2013 (PMID 24041432): moderate-to-severe motion in ~25% of stroke CTP patients, translations up to ~9-23 mm. Compute-today test: YES -- standard rigid registration tools, no annotator.
candidates.suspected_signal: Motion is patient behavior: severe cortical syndromes produce restlessness that survives motion correction as a textural residue; a model rewarded for predicting large infarcts in severe patients can learn the residue as a severity prior, exactly the acquisition-cue shortcut class DeGrave et al. documented in COVID radiography.
candidates.use_vs_association: Within-case paired injection: apply a calibrated per-frame rigid motion trace (amplitudes drawn from the cohort's own observed residual-motion distribution) to low-motion cases, re-run a standard motion-correction step so the model sees a realistically corrected-but-degraded series, hold every hemodynamic fact of the case fixed; a dose-response change in predicted final infarct, absent under a matched static-blur sham, distinguishes use of the motion signature from motion merely correlating with severity. Sign is itself identifying: PMID 34301804 shows motion pushes classical mismatch software toward SMALLER core estimates, while a learned severity prior predicts LARGER outputs under injected motion -- the two pathways point in opposite directions.
candidates.keystone_prerequisite: The released motion-corrected 4D CTP retains a measurable, patient-gradeable residual-motion signature (FD dynamic range above the re-registration noise floor).
candidates.keystone_evidence_note: The series sit inside the 99-GB train.7z; the prior cycle verified (DOI 10.1148/ryai.250603) that raw CTP is released motion-corrected and resampled to 1 frame/s, but no frame of it was opened today. If correction flattened the natural signal, the observational L1/L2 links weaken while the injection arm (which manufactures its own motion) still runs -- the claim then degrades from 'severity cue' to 'motion robustness audit', stated here in advance.
candidates.keystone_residual_assumption: Also assumed: the organizers' correction algorithm is close enough to a standard rigid pipeline that injected-then-corrected residue resembles natural residue texturally (mitigated by matching injected FD statistics to natural high-motion cases plus a real-vs-edited discriminator gate); and a competitive raw-CTP-ingesting baseline is trainable (shared assumption with baseline candidate c04).
candidates.dies_like_prior: Closest kill is idea-006 (extreme OOD intervention): answered by calibrating injected amplitudes to the cohort's observed distribution, passing edits through the same correction step, and a discriminator gate. The IDENTIFIABILITY_FAILURE pattern (ideas 009/016) is answered structurally: motion is a per-patient behavioral variable manipulated within-case with hemodynamics frozen, not a protocol constant varying only across sites. Adjacency disclosed: isles24-scout-001-c07 (truncation) and c08 (deconvolution fingerprint) are acquisition-quality cues at site/protocol level; this X is per-patient behavior, and site is held fixed by the within-case design.
candidates.closest_prior_work: Motion in stroke CTP is characterized (Fahmi et al. 2013, PMID 24041432) and its distorting effect on classical automated mismatch software is measured (PMID 34301804: smaller cores, larger penumbra under motion). Shortcut learning on acquisition cues is established in radiography (DeGrave et al., Nat Mach Intell 2021, DOI 10.1038/s42256-021-00338-7). Exact delta: no found work asks whether a learned stroke-outcome model responds to the motion signature itself -- the field's entire relationship to motion is corrective.
novelty_neighbors: Fahmi F et al., 'Head movement during CT brain perfusion acquisition of patients with suspected acute ischemic stroke', Eur J Radiol 2013 (PMID 24041432) -- quantifies motion prevalence and amplitude; no model audit.

'What is the impact of head movement on automated CT perfusion mismatch evaluation in acute ischemic stroke?' (PMID 34301804) -- motion biases classical threshold software; learned models and the severity-cue question untouched.

DeGrave AJ, Janizek JD, Lee S-I, 'AI for radiographic COVID-19 detection selects shortcuts over signal', Nat Mach Intell 2021 (DOI 10.1038/s42256-021-00338-7) -- the acquisition-shortcut genre, never applied to stroke CTP or to motion.
candidates.novelty_delta: Motion has been measured as a nuisance and corrected as an artifact, but no found work tests whether a trained final-infarct model uses the patient-motion signature as an informative feature, nor exploits the opposite-sign prediction that separates the shortcut pathway from the corrupted-hemodynamics pathway.
candidates.why_not_done: BLIND_SPOT: the field treats motion exclusively as noise to correct or a QC exclusion criterion, so nobody promoted it to a candidate feature; the actigraphy literature that treats movement as a behavioral vital sign never touches CT.
candidates.existing_assets: Released raw 4D CTP (motion-corrected, 1 frame/s) for 149 cases; released clinical CSV with admission NIHSS for the L1 check; FD is a standard formula atop standard registration tools; motion amplitude priors from Fahmi 2013; the cycle-shared baseline model.
candidates.smallest_decisive_experiment: Stage 0 (CPU only): FD and temporal-inconsistency census on all 149 corrected series, plus the L1 motion-NIHSS correlation from the released CSV. Decisive arm: on 40 low-motion held-out cases, inject motion traces at four amplitudes (25th/50th/75th/95th percentile of the observed distribution) plus a static-blur sham and a no-op resampling sham; forward passes through the shared baseline (raw-CTP channels perturbed, derived-map channels held fixed); primary readout is the paired, label-free change in predicted lesion probability mass, with sign interpreted against the PMID 34301804 direction.
candidates.compute_envelope: Fits one Colab GPU session given the cycle-shared checkpoint: registrations are CPU-parallel (~80 frames x 149 cases, hours on a standard VM, no GPU), and the decisive arm is ~40 x 7 = 280 forward passes, under 2 GPU-hours. The shared checkpoint itself is one separate A100 session (~8-12 h, reduced-epoch nnU-Net), counted once for the whole cycle.
candidates.standing_confounds_addressed: Within-case injection freezes patient, site, scanner, protocol, and hemodynamics; the static-blur sham separates average blur from frame-to-frame inconsistency; a spatially-incoherent temporal-noise sham matched in per-frame energy separates motion structure from generic noise; amplitude calibration plus the discriminator gate bound distribution shift. Not ruled out: the organizers' exact correction algorithm is unknown, so injected residue may differ texturally from natural residue -- the discriminator gate is the honest bound on this.
alternative_explanations: The model responds to any temporal inconsistency, not motion structure: the energy-matched incoherent-noise sham tests this.

Injected motion legitimately corrupts hemodynamic content and the prediction change is warranted: the opposite-sign benchmark (classical software shrinks cores under motion) plus holding derived-map channels fixed separates the pathways.

L1 fails in this cohort (motion uncorrelated with NIHSS): the finding degrades from severity-shortcut to motion-robustness audit -- still a certifiable property no challenge metric reports, stated in advance.
candidates.anticipated_negative: With the discriminator gate and a hemodynamic positive-control edit passing, a flat dose-response is a clean negative: the model is motion-robust across naturally occurring amplitudes -- a deployable robustness statement the challenge never tested, and a direct contrast with classical software's known fragility.
candidates.verified_dataset_facts: Relies on (verified 2026-08-16, scout_candidates.json dataset_verification): raw 4D CTP time series released per case, motion-corrected and resampled to 1 frame/s (Zenodo 16731717 description; DOI 10.1148/ryai.250603 carried from prior cycle); clinical data including admission NIHSS in the release (Zenodo description); 149 public training cases under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

clarity.why: One named signature and one injection test, but 'motion signature' bundles displacement and interpolation residue; the sham family unbundles it rather than the sentence.

identifiability.why: Opposite-sign pathways, within-case injection, and three shams isolate the cue well; the injected-versus-natural residue texture mismatch is the live residual.

medical_relevance.why: The sedation/intubation failure mode is a named deployment harm: triage models see ventilated patients, and a motionless severe stroke would be systematically under-scored.

interest.why: Inverts a universal assumption -- motion is information, not noise -- and either answer (shortcut found, or robustness certified against classical software's known fragility) lands with the imaging-AI audience.

prior_legwork.why: Motion amplitudes quantified, FD instrument standard, classical-software bias measured with a sign, NIHSS released; only the model and the census are new work.

feasibility.why: Capped: keystone NOT_INSPECTED (residual-motion dynamic range after the organizers' correction is unopened).

data_readiness.why: Public but the required raw series live in a 99-GB archive and the critical property is uninspected.

evaluation_readiness.why: Label-free paired deltas with standard gates; the signed external benchmark (PMID 34301804) is already published.

negative_result_value.why: A gated null certifies motion robustness at natural amplitudes -- a positive, publishable property, not an uninterpretable absence.

novelty_confidence.why: Capped by keystone status; targeted search found characterization and classical-software studies but no learned-model audit -- the novelty stage owns the verdict.

regret.why: The shortcut-learning genre is actively hunting new instances; motion in stroke CTP is sitting in the open with the clinical CSV needed to test it.

unverified_claims: Residual-motion dynamic range in the released corrected series
motion-NIHSS association in this cohort (L1, contested in literature)
trainability of a competitive raw-CTP-ingesting baseline
2021 Eur J Radiol baseline-features paper direction (paywalled today)

candidates.title: Little's law in the penumbra: the model may be reading the vasodilatory counterattack
candidates.question: Is an ISLES'24 model using the autoregulatory blood-volume reserve -- capillary beds held open while flow falls, CBV read against CBF -- to separate tissue that will survive reperfusion from tissue already lost?

cross_field.borrowed_construct: Control engineering: cerebral autoregulation is a feedback controller that defends delivery (CBF) by actuating vessel caliber; controller state is read from the ACTUATOR signal (CBV), not the controlled variable. Queueing theory supplies the bookkeeping: the central volume principle CBV = CBF x MTT is literally Little's law (L = lambda x W) -- a compensating region is a queue that lengthened to preserve throughput; a collapsed region has lost both.
cross_field.instrument_it_implies: A voxelwise actuator-state index: CBV relative to its mirror-homologous voxel, stratified by CBF decrement -- 'compensating' (rCBV_mirror >= 1 at reduced CBF) versus 'collapsed' (rCBV_mirror < 1) -- plus a Little's-law identity residual (does CBV = CBF x MTT hold in the released maps?) that both gates and disciplines the edits.
cross_field.what_changes_if_dropped: The measurement survives (CBV/CBF thresholds are classical stroke imaging), but the controller framing supplies the two-sided prediction (deviation-from-mirror sign, not CBV level) that separates construct use from generic channel use, and Little's law supplies the manifold constraint that keeps edits physiological.

candidates.deliverable_sentence: The final-infarct model is using the autoregulatory blood-volume reserve -- capillary volume held at or above mirror-normal while flow falls -- as its tissue-salvageability signal, distinguishing the still-compensating penumbra from the collapsed core at matched flow deficit.
candidates.X_measurement: rCBV_mirror = CBV / CBV_mirror per voxel from the released CBV maps registered to NCCT space, mirror via automatic midsagittal symmetry estimation, stratified by rCBF_mirror decrement. Clinical anchors: preserved autoregulation in penumbra produces vasodilation and normal-to-increased CBV while the core loses autoregulation and CBV collapses (Wintermark et al., Stroke 2006, DOI 10.1161/01.STR.0000209238.61459.39; review PMC2686422); the field later pivoted to rCBF<31% as the better core definition (Campbell et al., Stroke 2011, DOI 10.1161/STROKEAHA.111.618355), and a porcine CTP-PET study found the CBV infarction threshold varies with CBF -- the interaction beats either alone (PMC4922566). Compute-today test: YES -- released registered maps plus automatic mirroring; no annotator.
candidates.suspected_signal: Whether tissue is still defending itself is written in the actuator: at equal flow deficit, tissue with dilated, filled capillary beds is physiologically salvageable, while tissue whose blood volume has collapsed has lost microvascular integrity. Every training case -- final infarct conditioned on reperfusion -- showed the model the consequence of this difference.
candidates.use_vs_association: Within-case counterfactual that toggles the controller state: at fixed CBF and Tmax, move CBV inside the perfusion deficit between compensated (mirror-level) and collapsed (core-like) values, co-scaling MTT to preserve the Little's-law identity so edits stay on the physiological manifold; a paired, signed change in predicted final infarct under compensated-to-collapsed toggles, absent under off-deficit shams, distinguishes use of the reserve from CBV merely covarying with severity. A deliberate identity-VIOLATING probe (CBV moved without MTT) is run separately to ask whether the model even checks inter-map consistency -- informative either way, never pooled with the confirmatory arm.
candidates.keystone_prerequisite: Per-case CBV, CBF, MTT, and Tmax maps coexist co-registered in a common (NCCT) space so mirror indices and joint channel edits run automatically on every case.
candidates.keystone_evidence: Official repository (github.com/ezequieldlrosa/isles24, fetched 2026-08-16): derivatives contain 'Perfusion maps registered to NCCT space'; Zenodo record 16731717 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.16731717, fetched 2026-08-16) lists perfusion parametric maps (Tmax, CBF, CBV, MTT) per case with 'separate raw and co-registered derivative versions'.
candidates.keystone_residual_assumption: Still assumed: (1) the released maps approximately satisfy CBV = CBF x MTT -- vendor scaling can break the analytic identity, so Stage 0 measures the identity residual and, if it fails, co-edits follow the empirical joint (CBF,CBV,MTT) distribution instead; (2) mirror integrity (bilateral chronic disease, midline shift) -- per-case symmetry-quality flags, machinery shared with baseline c02; (3) a self-trained nnU-Net stands in for challenge submissions.
candidates.dies_like_prior: Closest kill is idea-016 (IDENTIFIABILITY_FAILURE via protocol): absolute CBV moves with injection protocol and cardiac output, but the mirror ratio and the within-case edits remove protocol by construction. idea-006 (OOD intervention) is answered by bounding toggles to the empirically observed rCBV_mirror range within cohort penumbra and core, manifold-consistent co-editing, and a discriminator gate. Adjacencies disclosed: baseline c02 asks what REFERENCE FRAME the model computes (contralateral normalization); c07 asks whether a specific physiological STATE read in that frame is used -- different X, shared mirroring machinery. isles24-scout-001-c01 (collateral clock) is upstream physiology: the CBV reserve is partly filled by collaterals, so the deliverable names the map-level signature (volume held up at low flow) and stays agnostic about whether autoregulatory dilation or collateral inflow fills it -- rung-honest wording, stated now.
candidates.closest_prior_work: The CBV-versus-CBF war for defining core was fought entirely with hand-set thresholds on patients (Wintermark 2006 for CBV; Campbell 2011 for rCBF; interaction evidence in PMC4922566) and then the field moved to end-to-end models (Robben et al., Med Image Anal 2020, PMID 31683091, arXiv:1812.02496 -- deconvolution-free prediction with metadata ablations; ISLES'24 report arXiv:2408.10966) without ever asking which side of its own debate the models internalized. Exact delta: channel-ablation studies remove whole input maps; nobody has toggled the physiological state the maps jointly encode while preserving their internal consistency.
novelty_neighbors: Wintermark M et al., 'Perfusion-CT assessment of infarct core and penumbra', Stroke 2006 (DOI 10.1161/01.STR.0000209238.61459.39) -- CBV-based core definition; human thresholds, no learned model.

Campbell BCV et al., 'Cerebral blood flow is the optimal CT perfusion parameter for assessing infarct core', Stroke 2011 (DOI 10.1161/STROKEAHA.111.618355) -- the debate's other side; still human thresholds.

Robben D et al., 'Prediction of final infarct volume from native CT perfusion and treatment parameters using deep learning', Med Image Anal 2020 (PMID 31683091, arXiv:1812.02496) -- end-to-end model with input/metadata ablations; no physiological-state manipulation within inputs.
candidates.novelty_delta: No found work tests whether an end-to-end final-infarct model uses the autoregulation-reserve construct -- CBV read against CBF at matched flow deficit -- as opposed to using CBV as one more severity channel; the two-sided mirror-referenced toggle is the new move.
candidates.why_not_done: BLIND_SPOT: the field litigated CBV-versus-CBF for human-defined core masks, declared rCBF the winner, and switched to end-to-end learning -- leaving unasked whether the models quietly re-adopted the losing (or a richer, interaction-form) construct.
candidates.existing_assets: Registered CBV/CBF/MTT/Tmax maps for 149 public cases; automatic symmetry-plane tools shared with baseline c02; exact published threshold numbers (CBV core, rCBF<31%, CBFxCBV interaction) to compare the model's behavior against; the cycle-shared baseline model.
candidates.smallest_decisive_experiment: Stage 0 (CPU): Little's-law identity-residual census and empirical joint (CBF,CBV,MTT) distributions in deficit versus mirror tissue on all 149 cases, plus a joint-support census (do both controller states occur at matched CBF decrement?). Decisive arm: 40 held-out cases, compensated-to-collapsed and collapsed-to-compensated toggles at three magnitudes plus off-deficit shams plus the identity-violating probe (~40 x 8 forward passes); primary readout is the paired, label-free, signed change in predicted lesion probability mass at matched CBF.
candidates.compute_envelope: Fits one Colab GPU session given the cycle-shared checkpoint: map arithmetic and mirroring are CPU-trivial; ~320 forward passes are under 2 GPU-hours. Cheapest wide candidate this cycle.
candidates.standing_confounds_addressed: Within-case edits hold patient, protocol, scanner, and site fixed; the mirror ratio removes global scaling (cardiac output, injection); matched-CBF stratification carries the observational arm; manifold co-editing preserves inter-channel consistency so the model cannot respond merely to a broken identity. Not ruled out: the reserve signature does not distinguish autoregulatory dilation from collateral inflow (deliberately absorbed into the claim's wording); perfusion-map smoothing across the deficit boundary (eroded ROIs); Tmax is held fixed although delay physiology is entangled with both states.
alternative_explanations: The model reads CBV as a generic monotone severity channel, not a reserve: a construct reader responds to the sign of deviation-from-mirror at matched CBF, a generic reader responds monotonically to CBV level including above-mirror values -- the two-sided toggle separates them.
The response is an edit artifact: discriminator gate, off-deficit shams, and physiologic-range bounds.

The model derives its prediction from Tmax alone and ignores the CBV/CBF/MTT triplet: then toggles do nothing while the Tmax positive control still moves the output -- itself a crisp channel-use finding.
candidates.anticipated_negative: With gates and the positive control passing, a null is a positive claim: the model's salvageability estimate ignores the blood-volume reserve, siding entirely with the rCBF camp of the field's oldest CTP debate -- a quotable statement about what benchmark models internalized, and a caution for anyone proposing CBV-derived inputs.
candidates.verified_dataset_facts: Relies on (verified 2026-08-16, scout_candidates.json dataset_verification): perfusion parametric maps (Tmax, CBF, CBV, MTT) per case with co-registered derivative versions in NCCT space (Zenodo 16731717 description; official repository derivatives listing); 149 public training cases, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; final-infarct ground truth from follow-up MRI conditioned on reperfusion (DOI 10.1148/ryai.250603, carried).

clarity.why: One construct, one signed two-sided test; 'reserve' requires the matched-CBF qualifier to be stated every time, which costs it the 5.

identifiability.why: Within-case toggles on the physiological manifold with sign predictions separate construct use from channel use; the collateral-versus-autoregulation ambiguity is absorbed into honest wording rather than resolved.

medical_relevance.why: Which tissue-fate construct the models internalize decides how their outputs should be trusted under hemodynamic variation, and speaks directly to the still-live CBV/CBF debate in core definition.

interest.why: Re-opens the field's foundational CTP debate inside its own benchmark models; the identity-checking probe (does the model know Little's law?) is a bonus hook.

prior_legwork.why: Thresholds, physiology, registered maps, and mirroring machinery all exist; only the shared model must be trained.

feasibility.why: Keystone INSPECTED_TRUE; parametric map edits and a few hundred forward passes -- the cheapest decisive arm this cycle.

data_readiness.why: Everything needed is in the public co-registered derivatives; noncommercial license.

evaluation_readiness.why: Label-free paired signed deltas with standard gates; published threshold numbers provide external comparison points.

negative_result_value.why: A gated null is a directional claim (pure-flow reliance) with a named consequence for CBV-derived input proposals.

novelty_confidence.why: Targeted search found the threshold literature and ablation studies but no state-toggle audit; held at 3 pending the novelty stage.

regret.why: The debate's numbers and the benchmark's models are one experiment apart; obvious in hindsight once stated.

unverified_claims: Little's-law identity residual in the released maps (vendor scaling)
joint support of both controller states at matched CBF in this cohort
mirror integrity rates in this cohort

candidates.title: Has the deficit percolated? Volume is what the metric sees; connectivity may be what the model uses
candidates.question: Is an ISLES'24 model using the percolation state of the hypoperfusion field -- whether Tmax-deficit voxels connect into one spanning cluster rather than scattered islands -- beyond the deficit's volume and severity?

cross_field.borrowed_construct: Site percolation from statistical physics: occupied sites form clusters; a spanning cluster appears abruptly at a critical occupation fraction; the order parameter is the largest-cluster fraction, and near-critical systems have diverging susceptibility -- tiny parameter changes produce large connectivity changes.
cross_field.instrument_it_implies: Threshold the released Tmax map at the clinical deficit definition (Tmax>6 s: Olivot et al., Stroke 2009, PMID 19109547, DOI 10.1161/STROKEAHA.108.526954), run 3D connected components (one-line scipy op), and read off the order parameter P_inf (fraction of deficit voxels in the largest cluster), cluster count, and distance-to-criticality (dP_inf as the threshold sweeps 4-10 s).
cross_field.what_changes_if_dropped: Connected-component counting survives as descriptive shape analysis, but percolation supplies the load-bearing predictions: an order parameter with an abrupt transition, and the near-threshold instability claim (L3) that turns a curiosity into an evaluation finding.

causal_chain.link: L1: At matched deficit volume and severity, natural variation in connectivity (P_inf) exists in this cohort.
causal_chain.separately_checkable_by: CPU census on all 149 released Tmax maps -- a gate, not an assumption.

causal_chain.link: L2: The model's predicted infarct extent tracks connectivity at matched volume and severity.
causal_chain.separately_checkable_by: The bridge/cut intervention below -- the use claim.

causal_chain.link: L3: If L2 holds, cases near the percolation threshold sit on a decision cliff: small severity perturbations flip large prediction changes, which the benchmark's per-case volume and lesion-count metrics then amplify.
causal_chain.separately_checkable_by: Prediction sensitivity to tiny global Tmax offsets (+/-0.5 s), plotted against distance-to-criticality.

candidates.deliverable_sentence: The model is using the connectivity of the hypoperfused region -- whether it has percolated into one spanning cluster -- as a determinant of predicted infarct extent beyond the deficit's volume and severity.
candidates.X_measurement: P_inf, cluster count, and distance-to-criticality from 3D connected components of the thresholded released Tmax map (Tmax>6 s primary, 4-10 s sweep), computed inside a parenchymal mask. Compute-today test: YES -- connected-component labeling on released registered maps; no annotator, no tool risk.
candidates.suspected_signal: Confluent and fragmented hypoperfusion are different diseases in the pattern literature (embolic showers versus territorial occlusion) with different fates; a model minimizing volumetric and lesion-wise losses on final infarcts has been rewarded for treating a spanning deficit differently from equal-volume scattered islands -- and ISLES'24's own lesion-wise F1 metric explicitly scores fragmentation of the output.
candidates.use_vs_association: Volume- and histogram-preserving topology edits: smooth, boundary-respecting, parenchyma-confined swaps of real multi-channel tissue signatures that either BRIDGE two large deficit clusters or CUT a thin isthmus, while conserving total deficit volume and the Tmax histogram via compensating opposite-signed local edits, all perfusion channels co-edited from the empirical joint distribution; a paired prediction difference between bridge and cut, absent under equal-volume random-relocation shams with identical local edit statistics, distinguishes connectivity use from volume/severity association.
candidates.keystone_prerequisite: Per-case Tmax and companion perfusion maps co-registered in a common space, enabling automatic connectivity computation and localized multi-channel edits.
candidates.keystone_evidence: Official repository (github.com/ezequieldlrosa/isles24, fetched 2026-08-16): derivatives contain 'Perfusion maps registered to NCCT space'; Zenodo record 16731717 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.16731717, fetched 2026-08-16) lists perfusion parametric maps (Tmax, CBF, CBV, MTT) per case with 'separate raw and co-registered derivative versions'.
candidates.keystone_residual_assumption: The load-bearing residual is edit realism: topology edits are the riskiest interventions this cycle because spatial rearrangement can leave statistical fingerprints even when histograms are conserved. Gates: spatial-autocorrelation matching, real-signature (not synthetic) swaps, discriminator, and a preregistered fallback -- if the edit gate fails, the candidate falls back to the observational matched-volume arm, which CANNOT claim use, stated now. Also assumed: L1 support exists (census gate) and enough cases have a bridgeable/cuttable geometry.
candidates.dies_like_prior: Closest kill is idea-006 (OOD intervention): answered by real-tissue-signature swaps, conservation constraints, autocorrelation matching, a discriminator gate, and the honest fallback above. The IDENTIFIABILITY_FAILURE pattern (idea-009: target inseparable from covarying anatomy) is answered by the intervention holding volume, histogram, location statistics, and anatomy fixed while only topology changes; the observational arm additionally matches on volume/severity and stratifies location. Adjacency disclosed: isles24-scout-001-c05 (spreading front) probes the internal gradient/front structure of the deficit; c08 probes global cluster topology at matched volume -- different X, different edit, and c05's backlog entry is cited to keep the boundary auditable.
candidates.closest_prior_work: Lesion-PATTERN epidemiology exists on outputs: scattered DWI patterns mark embolic etiology and predict outcome (PMID 16107355; the scattered-pattern literature descending from Baird et al. 2000). Percolation-flavored network modeling exists at capillary scale (oxygen-transport topology models, e.g. PMC4751405). The benchmark itself scores output fragmentation (lesion-wise F1; github.com/ezequieldlrosa/isles24 metrics list, verified). Exact delta: no found work measures tissue-scale percolation of the INPUT hypoperfusion field, and none tests whether a trained model responds to connectivity at fixed volume and severity.
novelty_neighbors: 'Specific DWI lesion patterns predict prognosis after acute ischaemic stroke within the MCA territory' (PMID 16107355) -- lesion-pattern prognosis on infarct outputs; no input-field connectivity, no model audit.

'Modelling the effects of cerebral microvasculature morphology on oxygen transport' (PMC4751405) -- network-topology physiology at capillary scale; different spatial scale, no imaging field, no learned model.

Robben et al., Med Image Anal 2020 (PMID 31683091) and the ISLES'24 report (arXiv:2408.10966) -- end-to-end models scored by volume/Dice/lesion-count; fragmentation appears only as an output metric, never as a tested input feature.
candidates.novelty_delta: Percolation has been applied to vessels at capillary scale and lesion patterns studied as output epidemiology, but no found work computes the percolation order parameter of the CTP deficit field or intervenes on its topology at conserved volume to test model use.
candidates.why_not_done: BLIND_SPOT: core/penumbra volumetrics monopolize both clinical decision rules and challenge metrics, so connectivity of the input field was never promoted from nuisance to variable. Search today was targeted, not exhaustive -- treat as NO_DUPLICATE_FOUND_LIMITED_SEARCH pending the novelty stage.
candidates.existing_assets: Registered Tmax and companion maps for 149 public cases; connected-component tooling in every scientific Python stack; the Tmax>6 s clinical threshold with primary citation; the benchmark's own lesion-wise F1 metric as motivation; the cycle-shared baseline model.
candidates.smallest_decisive_experiment: Stage 0 (CPU): threshold-sweep percolation census on all 149 cases -- P_inf, cluster counts, distance-to-criticality, and the L1 matched-volume variation check. Decisive arm: 30-40 held-out cases with at least two sizeable clusters or a cuttable isthmus; bridge/cut/sham triplets (~40 x 6 forward passes) plus the L3 sensitivity scan (+/-0.5 s global Tmax offsets, in-distribution by construction); primary readout is the paired difference in predicted lesion probability mass (continuous, never binarized) between bridge and cut at conserved volume.
candidates.compute_envelope: Fits one Colab GPU session given the cycle-shared checkpoint: the census is CPU-only; ~240 decisive forward passes plus the sensitivity scan are under 2 GPU-hours.
candidates.standing_confounds_addressed: Within-case paired edits hold patient, anatomy, site, and protocol fixed; conservation constraints (volume, histogram) remove the dominant covariates by construction; random-relocation shams control for local edit response; parenchymal masking prevents anatomically invalid bridges through CSF or ventricle; the L3 scan uses tiny global offsets rather than edits. Not ruled out: residual edit-realism fingerprints (the declared load-bearing residual), partial-volume voxels at cluster boundaries (eroded masks), and thin natural support for matched-volume topology variation (L1 gate decides).
alternative_explanations: The model responds to the local edit itself, not the topology change: random-relocation shams with identical local statistics but unchanged topology test this directly.
Connectivity proxies occlusion site or territory: the intervention holds anatomy fixed; the observational arm stratifies by territory.
Apparent discontinuity is thresholding in the readout, not the model: the primary readout is continuous probability mass, and the L3 claim is tested on prediction sensitivity, not binarized volumes.
candidates.anticipated_negative: With edit gates and a positive control passing, a flat bridge-versus-cut contrast says predicted extent is a local, integrative function of severity rather than topology -- which certifies the volume-centric reading, retires the near-threshold instability worry, and is directly useful to the challenge organizers who chose lesion-count metrics. Without the edit gate passing, the null is uninterpretable, and the fallback observational arm claims association only.
candidates.verified_dataset_facts: Relies on (verified 2026-08-16, scout_candidates.json dataset_verification): perfusion parametric maps including Tmax per case, co-registered to NCCT space (Zenodo 16731717 description; official repository derivatives listing); official ranking metrics include absolute lesion count difference and lesion-wise F1 (official repository, verified); 149 public training cases, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
candidates.design_template_note: The edit substitutes real multi-channel tissue signatures between regions of the same image under conservation constraints; regional-substitution is the closest named grammar, and choosing it over a fourth counterfactual-synthesis keeps the homogenization ledger honest without hiding the intervention's conservation structure, which is described in full above.

clarity.why: A named order parameter and a two-condition intervention; 'beyond volume and severity' is precise only because the conservation constraints are spelled out.

identifiability.why: When the edit gates pass, the bridge/cut contrast at conserved volume is clean; edit realism is the live risk and the fallback arm cannot claim use, so 3 until inspected.

medical_relevance.why: Predicted core volumes feed thrombectomy selection; if models sit on a connectivity cliff near the percolation threshold, the volumes clinicians receive inherit that instability in exactly the borderline cases where they matter.

interest.why: A model reading topology that the field's own volume metrics cannot see -- and the benchmark's lesion-count metric quietly rewarding it -- raises the intended eyebrow.

prior_legwork.why: Census tooling is trivial and the threshold is anchored, but there is no percolation-on-CTP literature to lean on and the edit machinery is new.

feasibility.why: Keystone INSPECTED_TRUE lifts the cap, but the topology-edit construction is the hardest engineering of the cycle; manageable, not days-to-first-result.

data_readiness.why: Registered public maps are all that is needed; the census runs the day the archive is open.

evaluation_readiness.why: Paired deltas are standard but the conservation-edit validity gates are custom and load-bearing.

negative_result_value.why: Decisive only behind the edit gate; the gated null is genuinely useful to the metric designers, the ungated one is not.

novelty_confidence.why: Targeted search found capillary-scale percolation and output-pattern epidemiology only; limited search, novelty stage owns the verdict.

regret.why: Speculative enough that the field may never miss it -- but the lesion-wise-F1 choice suggests the organizers are already circling fragmentation without naming it.
